problem: The four loose numbers (0.012, 0.02, 0.032, 0.375) appear with no code and no labels, so a student cannot tell what the 0.02 line is doing there — it merely repeats the M1 defect rate and is not a step result.
fix: Either drop the output block, or label each line with the step it belongs to, e.g. P(D ∩ A₁) = 0.012, P(D ∩ A₂) = 0.020, P(D) = 0.032, P(A₁|D) = 0.375.

problem: A base rate is defined as 'the prior P(A) when that prior is small'. The base rate is simply the unconditional prior (prevalence) whether it is small or large; only the striking effect needs a small prior.
fix: A base rate is the unconditional prior P(A), the share of cases in the population before any evidence. When it is small, it pulls the posterior down hard: a condition affects 1 person in 1000, so P(D) = 0.001.
